route: Residence permit for a private individual of independent means: para 7 (1) sentence 3 AufenthG ('In begruendeten Faellen kann eine Aufenthaltserlaubnis auch fuer einen von diesem Gesetz nicht vorgesehenen Aufenthaltszweck erteilt werden'). Para 5 (1) no. 1 requires secured livelihood, and para 2 (3) defines it: 'Der Lebensunterhalt eines Auslaenders ist gesichert, wenn er ihn einschliesslich ausreichenden Krankenversicherungsschutzes ohne Inanspruchnahme oeffentlicher Mittel bestreiten kann.' The foreign ministry's visa leaflet says cover must be 'ausreichende und auf Dauer angelegte private Krankenversicherung in Deutschland' taken out before entry; short 'Incoming' travel policies only cover the visa period.
policy: HanseMerkur 'Start Fit' (tariff KVS3 plus optional modules and Pflegepflichtversicherung PVN), full substitutive private health insurance, age-at-entry 45, EUR 1,000 annual deductible: outpatient, dental and inpatient; the modules priced include one- or two-bed room with chief-physician treatment (PSV), extra dental and cancer-test (EKV2), a Kurtagegeld (3.60) and statutory 10% surcharge. Germany (geographic scope not stated on the page). Unisex tariff, so same price for both partners. This is the insurer's self-employed tariff; the page does not say whether a non-employed person may buy it.
working: Insurer's own table, age 45: monthly total 590.30 EUR per person (KVS3 380.38 + PSV 46.76 + EKV2 25.65 + Kurtagegeld 3.60 + PVN care insurance 88.62 + statutory surcharge 45.29). Couple: 2 x 590.30 = 1,180.60 EUR per month.

typical_private.description: Basistarif at the legal ceiling for two adults (2 x 1,017.19 EUR, 2026). The ceiling is what most Basistarif members pay; it is the price of statutory-level benefits, higher than the HanseMerkur tariff because the Basistarif has no age or health pricing and is capped to the GKV maximum. Care insurance is billed separately (the BMG page gives no figure for it).

income_based_charges.name: Voluntary statutory (GKV) membership
income_based_charges.legal_source: SGB V para 240; access: a newcomer without prior German insurance and not employed generally cannot join the GKV (this is why PKV is modelled). Not used in the figure; for the tax agent only if some other route opens GKV.

eu_citizen_difference: An EU citizen exercising free movement who is a non-employed resident needs sufficient resources and comprehensive sickness cover under freedom-of-movement law, and can often keep S1/EHIC-based cover from a home state. A non-EU couple has no such route and must take a German substitutive PKV policy before entry.
spot_check: Basistarif ceiling 1,017.19 EUR per person (BMG) versus 590.30 EUR (HanseMerkur): the commercial tariff is 58% of the ceiling. HanseMerkur's own employee-tariff table (age 35) shows gross 569.73 EUR per person before the employer share, which is consistent with 590.30 at 45 for a thinner tariff. Not an independent insurer.
uncertainty: Single insurer figure. Eligibility of a non-employed couple for the self-employed tariff is unconfirmed; if only Basistarif is available the figure is about 2,034 EUR (+72%). Health underwriting: PKV can load or refuse for health history, and premiums rise with age and medical inflation (PKV-Verband and press report rises of about 13% for 2026, not checked here). The dated page may change. Residence permit success depends on the foreigners office; para 7 is discretionary. A GKV path was not priced.
